result.finding: Assessed 5 CWE rules in Credentials & Secrets: 3 FOUND, 2 NOT_FOUND
evidence: Scanned application source files for credentials & secrets patterns

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Password
values.description: The product contains a hard-coded password, which it uses for its own inbound authentication or for outbound communication to external components.

evidence.explanation: A plaintext SQL Server password is hardcoded at line 15 of batchscheduler.properties: 'db.******'. This file is packaged into the fat-jar at build time, meaning anyone with access to the jar can extract the credential. Although an environment variable override (SQLSERVER_PASSWORD) is supported, the default value remains committed to the repository.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key
values.description: The product uses a hard-coded, unchangeable cryptographic key.

values.name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
values.description: The product specifies permissions for a security-critical resource in a way that allows that resource to be read or modified by unintended actors.

values.name: Insufficient Logging
values.description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.

evidence.explanation: The application uses raw System.out.println for all logging (log() method, line 238). Security-critical events such as database connection failures (insertBatchRunLog catch block, ~line 135) and HTTP service call failures (callService catch block, ~line 93) are logged only as plain text messages with minimal context — no timestamp correlation with the batch run ID, no severity level, no structured fields. There is no logging framework (SLF4J, Log4j, Logback) configured, making it impossible to route security-relevant events to a SIEM or centralized log aggregation system.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
values.description: The product contains hard-coded credentials, such as a password or cryptographic key.

evidence.explanation: Both the SQL Server username and password are hardcoded in batchscheduler.properties: 'db.username=sa' (line 14) and 'db.******' (line 15). The username 'sa' is the SQL Server system administrator account — using this account for application connections violates the principle of least privilege. Both credentials are committed to version control and embedded in the application jar, exposing them to anyone with repository or artifact access.
